brief: A spending tracker where categories are geological layers — deeper is necessity, surface is discretionary

dominant_strengths: Strong conceptual metaphor — earth-tone strata genuinely map necessity-depth, making the palette do semantic work, not just decoration
Cohesive warm brown gradient feels tactile and geological, with category labels and totals reinforcing the cross-section illusion
Memorable framing ('Bedrock Foundation', 'Igneous Layer') gives reflective resonance rare in finance dashboards
dominant_weaknesses: Severe layout breakage — Entertainment row clipped at top, Bedrock Foundation cut at bottom, rows misaligned across layer boundaries
Progress bars are visually noisy and inconsistent: unclear if length encodes amount, budget cap, or category share, undermining behavioral utility
Typography hierarchy is flat — layer titles, descriptions, line items, and totals lack enough weight contrast to scan quickly
fix_priorities: Fix vertical rhythm and clipping so each strata band fully contains its rows with consistent padding
Define a single bar semantic (spent vs budget) with legend, and align all bar tracks to one grid
Tighten type scale: bolder layer headings, lighter descriptions, tabular-aligned dollar figures
Add subtle texture or fossil/sediment motifs only at layer seams to deepen metaphor without clutter
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral and reflective lead through the geological metaphor, but behavioral usability collapses under misaligned rows and ambiguous bars.
rationale.intent_fit: The concept executes the brief beautifully in principle, but compositional defects prevent it from functioning as a usable tracker.
